title: To establish the Office of Artificial Intelligence and Emerging Technology Threats within the Executive Office of the President, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
summary: This policy proposes creating a new Office of Artificial Intelligence and Emerging Technology Threats within the President’s Executive Office to monitor, assess, and mitigate risks posed by AI and other emerging technologies. It also includes additional, unspecified provisions aimed at strengthening national security and technology governance.

title: Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: The Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2026 is designed to ensure that AI systems are developed, tested, and deployed with high standards of safety, transparency, and accountability. It establishes regulatory frameworks and oversight mechanisms to promote trustworthy and reliable AI research and application.

title: CISA Securing AI Task Force Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: The CISA Securing AI Task Force Act establishes a federal task force to strengthen the security of artificial intelligence systems and technologies. It outlines measures for collaboration, risk assessment, and the development of guidelines to protect critical infrastructure and national security from AI‑related threats.

title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management and Security Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: This act establishes comprehensive guidelines for managing risks associated with artificial intelligence, including requirements for risk assessment, mitigation strategies, and continuous monitoring. It also sets up enforcement mechanisms and reporting obligations to ensure AI systems are secure and safe for the public.

title: Cybersecurity and AI Board of Investigations Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Cybersecurity and AI Board of Investigations Act of 2026 creates a federal board to oversee and investigate cybersecurity and AI-related incidents. The board will work with government agencies and private partners to identify threats, recommend safeguards, and coordinate protective responses.

title: A resolution establishing the Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence.
action: Referred to the Committee on Rules and Administration. (text: CR S5172-5174)
summary: The resolution establishes a Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence to study and advise on AI-related policy. The committee will investigate AI’s societal impacts, propose regulations, and monitor developments in the field.

title: Doctors Not AI Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committees on Ways and Means, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Doctors Not AI Act of 2026 mandates that medical diagnoses and treatments be performed by licensed physicians rather than automated AI systems, ensuring that human doctors retain primary decision‑making authority in clinical care. It imposes legal and regulatory barriers to the use of AI in healthcare settings, requiring human oversight, accountability, and compliance with established medical licensing standards.

title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Evaluation Act of 2025
action: Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs. Hearings held.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Risk Evaluation Act of 2025 establishes a framework for systematically assessing the risks posed by artificial intelligence systems. It requires developers and users to conduct thorough risk evaluations and report findings to a regulatory body, aiming to promote safety, accountability, and public trust in AI technologies.

title: CREATE AI Act of 2025
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 29 - 0.
summary: The CREATE AI Act of 2025 lays out rules for building and using AI, aiming to keep systems safe and trustworthy. The act requires companies to test AI for risks, disclose how they work, and gives regulators the power to enforce penalties if standards aren't met.

title: Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committee on Foreign Affairs, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act proposes a temporary pause on the construction and expansion of new AI data centers to address environmental and societal concerns. The act aims to allow for further study and the development of sustainable practices before resuming such projects.

title: Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, and in addition to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026 requires companies that design, build, or deploy AI systems to assess and report the environmental effects of their technologies, including energy use and carbon emissions. It establishes standards for minimizing these impacts, incentivizes the development of greener AI methods, and creates a federal oversight body to enforce compliance and promote transparency.

title: Make AI Work for Americans Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Finance.
summary: The Make AI Work for Americans Act is a proposed piece of legislation aimed at ensuring that artificial intelligence technologies are developed and deployed in ways that benefit the American public. The bill focuses on promoting responsible AI practices, protecting user privacy, and fostering innovation while preventing discrimination and misuse of AI systems.

title: K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions.
summary: The K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026 is a proposed law aimed at ensuring students and teachers have the knowledge and skills necessary to understand and responsibly use artificial intelligence. It establishes guidelines for integrating AI education into K‑12 curricula, provides teacher training resources, and promotes equitable access to AI tools across schools.

title: Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2025
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs.
summary: The Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2025 establishes standards and guidelines to ensure that AI systems developed under federal funding are safe, transparent, and accountable. It requires rigorous testing, documentation, and oversight throughout the research lifecycle to promote public trust and mitigate risks.

title: To direct the Secretary of Homeland Security, acting through the Director of the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, to establish a Critical Infrastructure AI Cyber Defense Pilot Program, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: This policy directs the Secretary of Homeland Security, through the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, to create a pilot program that uses artificial intelligence to protect critical infrastructure from cyber threats. It also includes additional, unspecified objectives related to enhancing national security and cyber resilience.

title: K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026
action: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 18 - 15.
summary: The K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026 aims to prepare students and teachers for an increasingly AI-driven world by requiring schools to integrate AI education into curricula, provide resources and training, and ensure equitable access to AI tools. The law seeks to promote AI literacy, critical thinking about technology, and responsible use of AI across all K‑12 educational settings.

title: VA Claims AI Accountability Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs.
summary: The VA Claims AI Accountability Act is a proposed law that would make sure artificial intelligence tools used in reviewing veterans’ claims are transparent, reliable, and fair. It sets rules and oversight to prevent bias, errors, and wrongful decisions that could negatively affect veterans’ benefits.

title: VA AI Transparency Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs.
summary: The VA AI Transparency Act of 2026 requires the Department of Veterans Affairs to clearly document and disclose the use of artificial intelligence in its programs, including the purpose, data sources, and intended outcomes of each AI tool. It mandates regular public reporting and stakeholder access to this information, so veterans and oversight bodies can understand how AI-driven decisions are made and assess potential impacts.

title: Artificial Intelligence Public Awareness and Education Campaign Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: This act proposes a nationwide campaign to increase public understanding of artificial intelligence, explaining its uses, benefits, and potential risks. It also requires the development and distribution of educational resources so that citizens can responsibly engage with AI technologies.

title: A resolution expressing the sense of the Senate regarding the importance of religious freedom, authoritative texts, and transparency in artificial intelligence systems.
action: Submitted in the Senate, considered, and agreed to without amendment and with a preamble by Unanimous Consent. (consideration: CR S4958; text: CR S4951)
summary: The Senate resolution underscores the importance of safeguarding religious freedom and respecting authoritative texts as guiding principles in the development and deployment of AI systems. It calls for increased transparency in AI to ensure these values are upheld and that stakeholders can understand how such systems operate.

title: Protecting Consumers from Deceptive AI Act
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 35 - 0.
summary: The Protecting Consumers from Deceptive AI Act aims to safeguard consumers by regulating AI that could mislead or deceive. It establishes guidelines and enforcement mechanisms to ensure transparency and honesty in AI applications.

title: To direct the Director of National Intelligence to submit to Congress a report on the use of artificial intelligence systems to acquire, analyze, query, disseminate, or otherwise access information under section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act of 1978.
action: Referred to the Committee on the Judiciary, and in addition to the Committee on Intelligence (Permanent Select), for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: This policy directs the Director of National Intelligence to present a report to Congress about how AI is used in surveillance under FISA Section 702. The report will cover AI’s role in gathering, analyzing, querying, distributing, and otherwise accessing information.

title: Artificial Intelligence Education and Workforce Readiness Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Education and Workforce, and in addition to the Committees on Science, Space, and Technology, and Ways and Means, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Education and Workforce Readiness Act of 2026 is a U.S. law that seeks to close the skills gap in the AI field by funding educational programs, research, and curriculum development. It aims to equip students, professionals, and the broader workforce with the knowledge and tools needed to thrive in an AI‑driven economy.

title: Open-Source AI Leadership Act
action: Ordered to be Reported by the Yeas and Nays: 26 - 21.
summary: The Open-Source AI Leadership Act is a proposed law that encourages the development of artificial intelligence using open-source technologies to promote transparency, accessibility, and innovation. It aims to create guidelines for collaboration, intellectual property, and ethical use of AI built on open-source platforms.

title: Stop AI Price Gouging and Wage Fixing Act of 2025
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committees on the Judiciary, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: This act aims to stop AI companies from charging excessively high prices and from manipulating labor markets to fix wages. It proposes regulatory measures to ensure fair pricing for AI services and protect workers’ wages.
